subject: PrivDeploy: access windows, key return timelines & subprocessor disclosure
messages:
From: Susan King <susan.king@novushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@novushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 May 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy: access windows, key return timelines & subprocessor disclosure

Hi Marcus / Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the private deployment walkthrough was helpful. As we move toward procurement I need to clarify a few items for our security and legal teams so we can finish the risk assessment:

- Access windows: Can you confirm the operational windows during which Redwood engineers may access the private control plane (e.g., scheduled maintenance windows, on-call emergency access)? We need clear SLAs and a maximum daily/weekly access budget to put in the DPA.

- BYOK key custody & return: If we supply a customer-managed CMK in our HSM, what is the documented process and maximum timeframe for Redwood to (a) request temporary operator unseal (for urgent remediation) and (b) return any escrowed artifacts after contract termination?

- Subprocessors: Please provide the list and the geographic regions of any subprocessors that would see telemetry or metadata for a private deployment (control-plane hosts, monitoring, backup). We primarily need to know if any subprocessors are outside the US/EU.

I’ve attached a short questionnaire (Novus_DPA_Qs.pdf) and would appreciate a single consolidated reply we can share with procurement. If easier, a brief call tomorrow morning would also work.

Thanks,
Susan King
Head of IT Security, NovusHealth
+susan.king@novushealth.com

Attachment: Novus_DPA_Qs.pdf (1 page)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Susan King <susan.king@novushealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: access windows, key return timelines & subprocessor disclosure

Susan — thanks for the clear list. I’m copying Irene (Security & Compliance) and Stephanie (Legal ops) so we can give single-source responses and attach the DPA draft + subprocessors sheet. Answers below are summary; please see the attached docs for the formal text we propose to put in the DPA.

1) Access windows / operator access policy
- Routine maintenance: Redwood will schedule non-disruptive maintenance windows and will provide at least 72 hours’ notice; these are typically during 02:00–06:00 local (your region) unless you request otherwise.
- Emergency access: In the event of an incident affecting availability or customer data integrity, Redwood engineers may request a temporary access window restricted to the minimum set of actions required to remediate. Emergency access requires: (a) documented justification, (b) prior approval from your on-call owner where possible, and (c) audit logging and post-access report delivered within 24 hours.
- Access budget: We typically agree a monthly operator access budget in the SOW; default at sign-up is 2 hours/month of human operator intervention unless otherwise contracted. Excess access is logged and billed at the agreed professional services rate or can be capped by policy.

2) BYOK custody and return timeline
- Customer-managed CMK: Redwood does not hold customer private key material unless explicitly requested for escrow. If you elect escrow, artifacts are encrypted and stored in our escrow HSM.
- Temporary unseal for remediation: Requests are handled via the break-glass playbook; Redwood will only perform unseal operations when authorized by an approved contact list and after multi-party approval (security + customer ops). We will provide a signed unseal justification and the operation log.
- Return/on-termination: If keys or escrowed artifacts exist, Redwood will return or securely destroy them within 7 business days of contract termination unless there is a legal hold. The DPA language in the attached draft puts this at 7–10 business days; open to your preference.

3) Subprocessors and telemetry exposure
- Attached: redwood_subprocessors_2025.xls — master list of subprocessors and region. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, only a small set of subprocessors touch metadata: (a) cloud market infra for control-plane hosting (if chosen), (b) monitoring/alert delivery service, (c) document signing provider. For strict on-prem installs with air-gap + customer control plane, exposure is zero.
- We flag any subprocessor outside the agreed geos and will include a subprocessor-add notice period in the DPA (30 days).

I’ve attached the DPA draft (privdeploy-dpa-draft.docx) with inline suggestions on wording for access budgets, operator controls, and key-return SLAs. If this looks good I can route to Contracts for a redline and we can schedule a 30-min sync to finalize.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: privdeploy-dpa-draft.docx, redwood_subprocessors_2025.xls
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Susan King <susan.king@novushealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: access windows, key return timelines & subprocessor disclosure

Susan — adding a few compliance-level clarifications and proposed DPA snippets inline below.

> Emergency access: In the event of an incident affecting availability or customer data integrity, Redwood engineers may request a temporary access window restricted to the minimum set of actions required to remediate.

Proposed snippet for DPA: "Redwood shall maintain an auditable operator access process. Emergency access shall only occur following documented incident triage, multi-party approval, and shall be limited in scope. All emergency actions will be recorded and a post-incident access report provided to the customer within 24 hours."

> Return/on-termination: ... return or securely destroy within 7 business days of contract termination unless there is a legal hold.

We prefer a deterministic timeline in the DPA: 7 business days for return, 30 days for destruction to allow for validated handover. We will include a certification of destruction or a cryptographic proof-of-erase for escrowed artifacts.

> Subprocessors: ... For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, only a small set of subprocessors touch metadata...

We will add a clause that for VPC-hosted private deployments the customer may opt into a "minimal telem" configuration that restricts monitoring payload to redwood-control-plane-liveness only (no application metadata) and that any subprocessor additions affecting this mode require explicit written approval.

Irene
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Marcus and Irene — this is exactly what we needed. Two quick asks before I share with procurement:

1) Can you update the DPA draft to state the 7 business day return + 30 day destruction timeline and include an example of the post-access report template?
2) Please confirm that the redwood_subprocessors_2025.xls is the "current as of" version and that Redwood will notify us 30 days before onboarding any new subprocessor that could see control-plane metadata.

If you can do the small edits today we’ll attach your responses to our RFP submission. Happy to run a 20-min call at 10:30 PT if that helps — Rajiv will be on the line for procurement sign-off.

Regards,
Susan
